first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel-health problems (activation -6% QoQ, onboarding completion -4% QoQ), and two independent inherited records point the same way: memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (signup field reduction produced a durable first-week activation lift in SMB). Convergent, mutually reinforcing evidence aimed directly at the observed regressions is the best fit for a single non-recurring slot, and it addresses a cause rather than papering over it. Promotional pricing is the obvious reflex given the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is explicitly caveated: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so the reported acquisition and revenue lift may be an artifact of the pooling rather than a real effect. Discount-led acquisition also carries downstream value risk against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue: it selects for the most price-sensitive, lowest-retention accounts, anchors expected price downward, and can inflate near-term revenue while degrading cohort quality — harm that would not surface within this experiment's window. I am spending verification on memory_73 precisely because it is the flagged one and because competitive pressure makes it the memory I am most likely to over-trust; if the archive shows the effect survives cohort separation, promotional pricing becomes a live option for a later slot. I am spending the second pull on memory_86 because it is the record I actually intend to act on, and an inherited summary is not the same as the original experiment record — I want to confirm the effect size, the population, and whether the lift persisted beyond early adoption before committing. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the supporting evidence is from days 12-52 and the current quarter's declines suggest conditions have shifted, so the prior may no longer hold at full strength. Uncertainty preserved: activation and onboarding declines may share an unmeasured common cause (traffic-mix shift from the competitor's launch pulling in worse-fit signups), in which case funnel simplification treats a symptom and the experiment should be read as diagnostic as much as corrective. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is plausible for pipeline quality but does not address the measured regressions; referral incentives (memory_57) act on established customers and will not move the self-serve funnel.
